headline: Beijing Student's Agent Engine Tops GitHub and Spawns a DeFi Fork
lede: Guo Hangjiang, a 20-year-old undergraduate at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, built a multi-agent social simulation tool called MiroFish in ten days and watched it reach number one on GitHub's global trending list. Within 24 hours of a demo video, a Chinese billionaire committed roughly $4 million to back the project. A DeFi builder then forked the repository, added a simulated prediction-market layer, and released MiroShark — extending an already extravagant narrative with fresh architecture.
body:
Guo Hangjiang is a senior at **Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications** who built *MiroFish* using a style of rapid, AI-assisted development its advocates call *vibe coding*. Released on March 7, 2026, the repository reached number one on GitHub's global trending chart within hours, surpassing projects from better-funded teams. The tweet's star count (~33,000) reflects a mid-March snapshot; the repository has since grown to roughly 59,000 stars. Guo's prior project, *BettaFish* — a multi-agent sentiment analyzer — had similarly topped GitHub trending in late 2025, catching the attention of a prominent investor.

What MiroFish actually does is less prediction engine than scenario explorer. A user feeds it a seed document — a news article, a policy draft, a financial filing — and the system uses *GraphRAG* (Microsoft's (MSFT) graph retrieval-augmented generation framework) to extract entities and relationships into a knowledge graph. It then instantiates hundreds to thousands of AI agents, each assigned a unique personality and social connections, and runs them across simulated Twitter-like and Reddit-like environments. The underlying framework is *OASIS* (Open Agent Social Interaction Simulations), an academic project maintained by the CAMEL-AI research community that can model up to one million interacting agents. The recommended language model is Alibaba's (BABA) Qwen-plus, accessed via the Bailian cloud platform. A Report Agent synthesizes the emergent behavior into a narrative summary.

Within 24 hours of seeing the demo, Chen Tianqiao — founder of Shanda Group, once China's wealthiest man and now a technology investor — committed 30 million RMB (~$4.1 million) to incubate the project, elevating Guo from intern to CEO overnight. Chen promotes what he calls the “super individual” thesis: that AI now lets one person accomplish what previously required an entire company. He reportedly acknowledged that BettaFish's technical level was not exceptional, but valued Guo's instinct for identifying problems worth solving.

The fork is where the architecture becomes interesting. Aaron Mars, co-founder of Hyperstitions — a coordination platform built on the Monad blockchain that routes capital into live prediction markets — forked MiroFish and released *MiroShark*. His key addition is a third simulated environment modelled on a prediction market, running a *constant-product AMM* (an automated pricing mechanism borrowed from DeFi protocols, where price shifts as agents buy and sell shares in a given outcome). A “Market-Media Bridge” feeds social-media sentiment into trader-agent prompts and pushes prices back into social posts in real time. Mars also replaced the cloud-based Zep memory layer with Neo4j, a self-hosted graph database, and targeted a $1-per-run cost floor. One important clarification: MiroShark's prediction market is entirely simulated — there is no on-chain component, and its roughly 1,100 stars are a fraction of the parent project's reach.

The critical case is worth stating plainly. No published benchmarks compare either system's outputs against real-world outcomes. Because both are probabilistic, identical seed documents can yield different results on successive runs, making systematic validation difficult. Researchers have flagged that LLM-powered agents tend toward *herd behavior* — forming consensus more readily than real human populations — which can distort simulations of polarization or surprise events. An independent case study rated MiroFish 5.54 out of 10, flagging unproven prediction accuracy and single-point-of-failure founder risk. The claim to “predict anything” is promotional; what both systems generate is more accurately described as plausible narratives about how simulated populations might respond to a given stimulus.

concepts.definition: A style of rapid, intuition-driven software development in which the programmer relies heavily on AI coding assistants rather than writing every line by hand. The term emphasizes speed and creative momentum over engineering rigor, and has become associated with solo founders building viral prototypes quickly.

A computational model in which many autonomous software agents — each with distinct rules, goals, and memory — interact within a shared virtual environment. Researchers use these models to study how complex social behaviors such as rumor spreading, market panics, or opinion formation emerge from individual-level decisions.

Microsoft's extension of retrieval-augmented generation that first converts source documents into a knowledge graph — a network of entities and their relationships — before using that structure to answer queries or initialize agent behaviors. This lets the model reason across relational structure rather than treating a document as a flat block of text.

Open Agent Social Interaction Simulations, an academic simulation engine maintained by the CAMEL-AI research community. It can model up to one million AI agents interacting on social media-like platforms, supporting 23 action types such as posting, liking, and following. MiroFish uses OASIS as its underlying simulation infrastructure.

An automated market maker — an algorithmic pricing engine — where the product of the quantities of two assets in a pool must remain constant. As traders buy one side of a market, its price rises and the other falls, automatically. This mechanism underlies many DeFi protocols and is used in MiroShark to price simulated prediction-market shares.

Platforms where participants buy and sell contracts whose payoff depends on the outcome of a real-world event. Prices function as crowd-sourced probability estimates. Polymarket and Kalshi are dominant venues as of 2026 and have shown competitive accuracy against professional forecasters on well-defined binary questions.

In agent-based modeling, the tendency of individually rational agents to converge on the same conclusions because they share similar information and reasoning processes. In LLM-powered simulations the problem is acute: the underlying models are nearly identical, producing artificial consensus that would not appear in a real, heterogeneous population.

Decentralised Finance — financial services including lending, trading, derivatives, and prediction markets built on public blockchains and governed by smart contracts rather than banks. Transactions settle automatically without a central intermediary.

repos.summary: MiroFish is a multi-agent swarm intelligence engine that generates hundreds of AI agents from a seed document and runs them across simulated social media environments to produce scenario-based predictions. Built in ten days by Guo Hangjiang using the OASIS simulation framework, Microsoft GraphRAG for knowledge extraction, and Alibaba's Qwen-plus as the recommended language model. It reached number one on GitHub's global trending list in March 2026 and has accumulated roughly 59,000 stars.

MiroShark is a fork of MiroFish by DeFi builder Aaron Mars that adds a simulated prediction-market environment running a constant-product AMM alongside the standard social-media platforms, with a Market-Media Bridge that feeds sentiment into prices and prices back into posts. It replaces MiroFish's cloud-based Zep memory system with a self-hosted Neo4j graph database and supports any OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint, targeting roughly $1 per simulation run. The prediction market is entirely simulated; there is no on-chain component.

fact_check: The tweet describes Aaron Mars as a 'DeFi trader' who forked MiroFish and built something the original never delivered. Mars is more accurately a DeFi founder — co-founder of Hyperstitions, a live prediction-market coordination platform — and a venture capital investor, not primarily a trader. More substantively, the implication that MiroShark delivers real prediction-market functionality is misleading: its prediction market is entirely simulated, with no blockchain or live capital at risk. Mars's live DeFi work, Hyperstitions, is a separate project. The framing exaggerates the distinction between the two tools.
